requestedOutcome: Identify and fix the remaining Metal pixel differences, without increasing tolerance or substituting software rendering.

environment.renderer: ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M5 Pro, Unspecified Version)

fixedFindings.title: Submit immediate draws and external-consumer boundaries
fixedFindings.cause: The render loop did not distinguish ticker draws from immediate redraw/flush calls. Immediate WebGL rendering and onAfterRender consumption had no explicit command-submission boundary.
fixedFindings.change: Render phases are explicit; submit WebGL commands before the external consumer and after immediate drawing, preserving ordinary animation ticks without an explicit flush.
fixedFindings.limit: gl.flush submits work; it is not a GPU completion wait and does not solve the residual WhiteCat mismatch.

fixedFindings.title: Replace varying fragment UV derivatives with affine triangle gradients
fixedFindings.cause: The first observed GPU mismatch is dFdy(UV); mip filtering then returns different sampled colors. CPU/Worker frame equality alone cannot establish GPU pixel equality.
fixedFindings.change: Use a triangle Jacobian carried in a flat attribute with textureGrad; retain shared vertices and reusable owned buffers.
fixedFindings.after: Zero different channels in all 8 stages for SSAA, MSAA, main-thread/Worker and development-model comparisons.

experiments.name: native-commands
experiments.observation: All 4876 final-frame write calls match, including uploaded bytes. GL object references have a bijection over 205 objects; this is not a comparison that merely removes all object identities.

experiments.name: shadow-state
experiments.observation: 405 draws: lifetime CPU shadows of attribute/index buffers and effective uniform values match. Buffer hashes are FNV-1a, not bytewise GPU readback.

experiments.name: textures
experiments.observation: Two 8192x8192 source images and all 14 mip levels match by readback hash after the differing frame.

experiments.name: padding
experiments.observation: 94 end-of-frame textures: only the final back buffer and one 64x32 copied backdrop differ. The two bytes in that backdrop are inside its copied 42x18 area and correspond to already-different source pixels at (470,136) and (469,137); not stale padding.

experiments.name: shaders
experiments.observation: All 13 GLSL shader sources match exactly.

experiments.name: single-pass
experiments.observation: One asynchronous PBO sample after draw 100 removes the buffer-off mismatch, but burst still differs. This is an observer effect, not an accepted fix.

experiments.name: before-color-original
experiments.observation: Adding a submission boundary before the scene does not fix all stages.

experiments.name: copy-blit
experiments.observation: Replacing backdrop copyTexSubImage2D with NEAREST framebuffer blits does not fix all stages.

experiments.name: dither-init
experiments.observation: Disabling DITHER from context creation does not fix the mismatch.

experiments.name: orphan
experiments.observation: Orphaning ARRAY_BUFFER storage before updates does not fix all stages.

experiments.name: grad
experiments.observation: Explicit derivatives in the batch sampler do not fix all stages.

experiments.name: invariant-matched
experiments.observation: Matching highp/invariant varying declarations does not fix the mismatch.

experiments.name: flat-mesh
experiments.observation: Flat per-triangle colors and texture IDs in GLSL 300 mesh/batch shaders do not fix the mismatch.

experiments.name: color-direct
experiments.observation: Algebraically equivalent premultiplied color matrix evaluation does not fix all stages.

experiments.name: copy-flush
experiments.observation: Submitting before backdrop copies does not fix the mismatch.

experiments.name: finish
experiments.observation: Forcing GPU completion in place of submission does not fix the mismatch. No finish/readback was added to production.

experiments.name: float-targets
experiments.observation: RGBA32F intermediates do not fix the mismatch. No format or memory changes were added to production.

experiments.name: validated-stderr
experiments.observation: Metal API and GPU validation are explicitly confirmed enabled in stderr; no resource-access or load/store validation fault was reported, while the strict pixel comparison still fails.

nativeDiagnostics.mslObservation: ANGLE_METAL_PRINT_MSL_ENABLE captured native translated Metal source. WEBGL_debug_shaders returned empty strings; those empty values were not treated as proof of translated-code equality.
nativeDiagnostics.frameCapture: The installed release Chrome binary does not expose the ANGLE_METAL_FRAME_CAPTURE environment hook. A native frame debugger/replay capable of identifying the first differing GPU operation is still required; shader text and API traces alone did not establish it.

outOfScopeVerification: Other devices and browsers; low-end performance; long-duration retained-memory profiling.

firstObservedGpuDivergence.backend: ANGLE Metal on Apple M5 Pro, Chrome 156
firstObservedGpuDivergence.operation: dFdy(vUV) in the first batched mesh draw
firstObservedGpuDivergence.measurement: UV, derivatives and sampled RGB were written to independent RGBA32F attachments in the same actual GPU draw; color writes to those attachments were disabled after that draw. Readback occurred after the captured prefix.
firstObservedGpuDivergence.interpretation: Finite-difference UV gradients vary despite identical center UV and uploaded geometry. The different sampling footprint changes mip filtering. An analytic triangle Jacobian removes this source of variation.
firstObservedGpuDivergence.limit: Shader-stage GPU tracing, not a native ISA debugger. No generic Metal driver defect is claimed.

implementation: Compute the affine UV Jacobian from the packed Float32 triangle coordinates, using JS arithmetic before storing the result as Float32.
Send it as a flat vertex attribute and use textureGrad with the screen-space Jacobian.
Keep shared vertices and add one provoking vertex per triangle; select FIRST when the extension is available, otherwise LAST.
Reuse vertex and index capacity; refresh indices when source vertex counts change; release owned geometry and shaders with their source/renderer.
gpuSamplingFollowUp.comparisonContract: The final shader is checked for repeat-render and main-thread/Worker pixel identity. This does not assert byte identity between the old implicit-gradient filter and the intentionally corrected analytic-gradient filter. No pixel tolerance was introduced or increased.
